definition: Sum of requested numResults across 7 Exa search calls, NOT 83 fully read independent papers.

sources.title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers
sources.horizon: Formation and holding 3–12 months; some specifications skip one week.
sources.finding: Past winners minus losers show intermediate-horizon return continuation; short-run reversal is explicitly a separate effect.
sources.costs: Main evidence is gross portfolio returns; skipping a week reduces microstructure effects but does not establish next-open 5-day net profitability.
sources.position: Diversified long-short decile portfolios, not three long-only picks.
sources.implementation: Hypothesis only: intermediate relative-strength feature with appropriate history. A 20-day return is not this validated signal.
sources.limits: No 5-day +10% or loss-free claim. Winner-leg results must be measured independently.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed foundational original paper, university-hosted full text.
sources.replication: Jegadeesh–Titman 2001 / NBER 1999: out-of-sample momentum continued in 1990–1997; same medium-horizon family.

sources.title: The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing
sources.horizon: Current price / previous 12-month high; portfolios held six months (also examine 12-month holding).
sources.finding: Nearness to 52-week high explains a large share of conventional momentum; stronger conditional explanatory power outside January.
sources.costs: No verified net cost-adjusted five-day estimate in retrieved paper.
sources.position: Long top 30% ratio and short bottom 30%, overlapping portfolios.
sources.implementation: Use actual trailing 252-trading-day high only if history exists; near-high and breakout tests separate. Shorter 20/60-day high is a new hypothesis.
sources.limits: Does not imply buying a fresh breakout tomorrow earns +10% within a week.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed original paper on author's university page.

sources.title: Price Momentum and Trading Volume
sources.sample: NYSE/AMEX January 1965–December 1995; NASDAQ holdout discussed separately.
sources.horizon: Past J-month returns and average daily turnover; holding 3, 6, 9, 12 months and long-run reversals.
sources.finding: Volume helps identify momentum stage and reversal speed; low-volume winners can outperform high-volume winners, and high-volume winners reverse sooner. Not a monotone volume-buy signal.
sources.costs: Short-horizon bid-ask effects reduced by skipping a week/month; no established five-day net edge.
sources.position: Return deciles crossed with turnover tertiles; long-short portfolios.
sources.implementation: Treat volume regime as interaction, not an unconditional reward. Daily volume / 20-day average is not share turnover.
sources.limits: Historical paper excludes firms delisted within five days of formation; avoid reproducing this future-information filter.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed original full text hosted by asset manager associated with research; practitioner hosting is not independent replication.

sources.title: Short-term Momentum
sources.sample: US NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ common nonfinancial shares, July 1963–December 2018; international and earlier-US robustness.
sources.horizon: Previous calendar-month return and share turnover; next-month holding, monthly rebalancing.
sources.finding: High-turnover stocks show monthly momentum while low-turnover stocks reverse; strongest for large liquid well-covered stocks. Crucially authors report average WEEKLY short-term momentum returns are negative.
sources.costs: Monthly result survives conservative estimated transaction costs; does not establish weekly profitability.
sources.implementation: Use turnover/liquidity interactions only as hypotheses for Korean five-day validation; OHLCV relative volume cannot exactly replicate turnover without shares outstanding.
sources.limits: Direct negative weekly evidence means monthly result cannot validate the requested horizon.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed RFS original full text in university repository.

sources.title: 한국주식시장의 단기반전과 단기모멘텀
sources.sample: Korean stocks; precise start/end dates not available in accessed abstract.
sources.horizon: Prior-month return / turnover groups, monthly short-horizon effects.
sources.finding: Finds short-term reversal but no high-turnover short-term momentum, unlike Medhat–Schmeling. Reversal survives size, microstructure/arbitrage-constraint and T+2 controls, strongest small illiquid stocks.
sources.costs: Cost-adjusted implementable three-stock performance not established in abstract.
sources.position: Sorted portfolio factor study, not daily three-stock signal.
sources.implementation: Explicit local counter-evidence against naively transferring US high-turnover winners; test same-horizon Korean holdout.
sources.limits: Abstract-only evidence; do not invent exact sample or cost model.
sources.quality: Original Korean journal article abstract on journal distribution service; full paper not accessed.

sources.title: Momentum and reversal effects in the Korean stock market
sources.horizon: Momentum/reversal portfolio horizons; precise formation/holding parameters not verified from accessible abstract.
sources.finding: Individual-stock momentum mostly exhibits reversal; industry momentum generally insignificant; momentum appears in some subperiods but reversal dominates after risk controls.
sources.costs: No verified transaction-cost result in accessed abstract.
sources.implementation: Require Korea/time-regime validation; a US industry-momentum paper is not sufficient support.
sources.limits: Abstract-only. Do not infer that every particular five-day breakout strategy is disproved.
sources.quality: Original peer-reviewed journal abstract; accessible via journal distributor.

sources.title: The Momentum Investment Strategy in the Korean Stock Market
sources.sample: Korea; comparisons around Asian financial crisis; exact dates not in accessed abstract.
sources.horizon: Traditional and 52-week-high momentum; exact holding parameters not in abstract.
sources.finding: 52-week-high momentum outperforms traditional momentum, with strong seasonality and structural-period sensitivity.
sources.costs: No verified after-cost result in accessed abstract.
sources.position: Momentum portfolio study; not three-stock selection.
sources.implementation: Near-high is more locally grounded hypothesis than blindly chasing largest recent returns; retain seasonal/regime scrutiny.
sources.limits: Older context, abstract-only, no evidence for five-day +10%.
sources.quality: Original research abstract in Korean national research index.

sources.title: Residual Momentum
sources.sample: US CRSP January 1926–December 2009; 36-month trailing factor regressions.
sources.horizon: 12-minus-1-month residual returns, standardized by residual volatility; holding 1–12 months.
sources.finding: Residual ranking reduces time-varying market/size/value exposure and roughly doubles risk-adjusted performance relative to raw momentum; substantial drawdowns remain.
sources.costs: Lower small-cap exposure may reduce costs; direct cost advantage is not guaranteed by the abstract.
sources.implementation: Market-relative return is a simple OHLCV-compatible hypothesis, but not identical to Fama–French residual momentum. Exact replication needs factor history and long estimation windows.
sources.limits: Not a weekly breakout signal or no-loss rule; original study reports residual drawdowns about 40% in post-2000 episode.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed original accepted manuscript in Erasmus repository; authors associated with Robeco.
sources.replication: 2017 author/practitioner follow-up reports global and post-publication robustness; not independent of original research team.

sources.title: Time series momentum
sources.sample: 58 liquid equity-index, currency, commodity and bond futures, January 1985–December 2009.
sources.horizon: Persistence 1–12 months; main rule 12-month lookback, one-month holding.
sources.finding: Diversified time-series trend portfolio shows strong results across futures and performs well in extreme markets.
sources.costs: Liquid futures setting and lower-frequency trading differ materially from Korean small stocks; no five-day stock cost claim.
sources.position: Diversified long-short futures with volatility scaling, not three cash equity longs.
sources.implementation: Market trend/regime feature is a research hypothesis; do not claim daily stock model is this strategy.
sources.limits: Asset, horizon, leverage and diversification mismatch. AQR-affiliated authors' strategy evidence is not proof of user target.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed original paper on university author page; practitioner affiliations disclosed.

sources.title: Momentum Strategies
sources.sample: US equities, January 1977–December 1993; monthly sorts start through January 1993.
sources.horizon: Past six-month returns and earnings surprises; subsequent six/twelve-month drift.
sources.finding: Past return and past earnings surprise each predict later drift controlling for the other; sluggish analyst responses support gradual information incorporation.
sources.costs: No verified five-day net implementation or execution model from accessed sections.
sources.implementation: Cannot implement earnings-surprise strategy from OHLCV alone. Requires timestamped actual/consensus or earnings history available before recommendation.
sources.limits: News proximity is not positive earnings surprise; no retrospective event labels.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed original full text on university site; NBER primary working-paper landing page available.

sources.title: Are Momentum Profits Robust to Trading Costs?
sources.sample: CRSP February 1967–December 1999; price-impact estimation uses TAQ January 1993–May 1997.
sources.horizon: 2/5/11-month ranking; one-month skip; 1/3/6/12-month holding. Focus winner-only 11/1/3 and 5/1/6.
sources.finding: Gross equal-weight momentum can rank best yet net of impact rank worst; liquidity-weighted and hybrid portfolios have greater capacity. Authors deliberately analyze winner-only implementation.
sources.costs: Explicit spreads, commissions, nonlinear impact; supports capacity-sensitive survival for certain monthly strategies, not all.
sources.position: Includes long-only winner portfolios, more relevant than long-short evidence but many names.
sources.implementation: Use liquid, executable universe and next-open entry; report cost-adjusted exit returns and fill limitations, not intraday high as realized gain.
sources.limits: Historical US cost estimates do not determine current Korean fees/taxes/spreads.
sources.quality: Peer-reviewed original paper hosted on author's university site.

sources.title: Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap
sources.horizon: Many moving-average, support/resistance, filter and channel-breakout rules with varied daily rules, not a five-day equity stock picker.
sources.finding: Some 1897–1986 technical-rule profits survive data-snooping adjustment, but evidence is scant in 1987–1996 out-of-sample. Tests roughly 8,000 rule variants.
sources.costs: Considers next-day signals and futures to examine implementability; historical in-sample significance is not production assurance.
sources.implementation: Predefine a small candidate set, preserve untouched chronological test, evaluate next-open trades; no selecting best of many thresholds on test.
sources.limits: Breakout premise alone is not validated modern five-day Korean stock edge.
sources.quality: Original scholarly working paper in LSE repository, later Journal of Finance.
sources.original: Brock–Lakonishok–LeBaron 1992 original: moving-average/trading-range-break evidence in DJIA 1897–1986; original paper accessed via mirror.
sources.replication: Fang–Jacobsen–Qin 2012 original working-paper abstract: exact earlier rules fail in true out-of-sample 1987–2011.

additional_primary_sources.title: Do Industries Explain Momentum?
additional_primary_sources.finding: Original US paper: industry momentum explains much stock momentum; Korean 1983–2023 replication above finds no general industry effect. Abstract read; no precise sample asserted.

additional_primary_sources.title: Stock Price Reactions to News and the Momentum Effect in the Korean Stock Market
additional_primary_sources.finding: Original abstract: overall Korean momentum profits absent; news losers drift down, winners reverse; costs matter. News alone does not justify buying winners.

additional_primary_sources.title: 한국 주식시장에서의 실적 발표 기간의 단기 반전 효과
additional_primary_sources.finding: Original abstract: significant short-term reversal concentrated ahead of earnings announcements, linked to liquidity-provider inventory risk. Requires event timestamps; not generic bullish news rule.

implementation_conclusions: No paper establishes three daily Korean picks each reaching +10% within five trading days without loss.
Existing score >=70 is a user eligibility constraint, not an empirically validated probability. Do not rescale/inflate scores.

Start with fixed high-score, liquid, healthy-trend candidates; test near-high and relative-strength/volume-interaction hypotheses against that exact universe. Any threshold choice remains empirical, not prescribed by these papers.
Strongest immediate negative evidence: monthly high-turnover momentum paper itself reports negative weekly momentum on average; Korean high-turnover replication is negative.
Evaluate actual executable next-open to defined exit, costs, D5 net returns, loss frequency/tails, and drawdown alongside intraday +10% touch. Touch does not establish realizable profit.
Raw volatility rewards select both sharp rises and crashes; risk and expected gain must be distinguished.
Freeze test dates and candidate family before evaluating; no outcome-specific repeated tuning disguised as validation.
Unavailable earnings/float/industry/252-day/factor inputs must not be silently replaced with proxies while claiming replication.
